# Student invitations

The module owns the invitation side of the org [seats](../../../.github/.github/instructions/seats.instructions.md) doc: the rows a teacher adds, the email, the claim that joins a student to the course, the approvals, and the managed-account record. That doc owns the flows, states and rules; this one owns what the module decides in carrying them out. Seats themselves live in the choreographer, which asks the module which invitations a student has claimed. The earlier per-address course invitations of [invite_by_email](invite-by-email.instructions.md) are a separate store and are left as they are.

## Decisions

- **One row per course and address.** Addresses are compared on a canonical key, so a re-typed or re-cased address is the same row. Adding an address that is already live changes nothing; adding one that was revoked or left starts a fresh invitation with earlier decisions cleared.
- **The invite email is the class link plus the invitation id.** The class code still joins the course on its own; the id only adds the invitation step. An email is sent only while the row's send count still equals the one the teacher saw, so a second click or a second tab sends once. A send stops early when the mail service itself fails, because the rest would fail the same way. The email's Canvas line stays off until Canvas is released.
- **Invite to a seat.** For a joined student with no invitation, a row is made from the student's own first address with no email sent. Neither the teacher nor the caller ever sees that address.
- **The claim is one path for every way in**: the student opening the invitation, the teacher's Grant and Approve all, sign-in or a newly verified address, and the Canvas link step. A claim needs a verified matching address, the teacher's grant, or the Canvas identity the row was imported with; there is no separate confirmation step. The account is joined to the course first, then one transaction claims the row only if it is still Invited and the account holds no other joined invitation in the course. A join left behind by a refused claim is harmless, since a class-code join is allowed. Two claims of one row cannot both win, and no other service matches an address to an account.
- **A request is recorded only for a different address.** Opening an invitation without the invited address verified records a request for the teacher, who sees the address that account signed up with; only course admins ever do. An account already joined in the course that opens another invitation there is refused with a conflict and nothing is recorded, because identity is the account, not the link.
- **Managed exactly while not an admin.** Each claim records the managed account unless the claimant is an admin of that course or a server admin. The module follows the course's power levels, so the record appears or disappears as a claimant stops or starts being an admin, and each sign-in re-applies the rule to repair a missed event.
- **Leaving ends the invitation.** Leaving, being kicked or being banned sets the invitation Left, which ends its seat at the choreographer's next check.
- **One history.** Every invitation change is recorded in an append-only history, read by admin-dash-api for the Seats tab's Activity, in the same transaction as the change. A sent email is the exception: it is recorded after the mail service accepts it, and a failed record is reported rather than failing a send that already went out.
- **Privacy.** Teacher routes re-check course admin on every request and refuse with one identical answer, so a route says nothing about which rooms exist. The public sign-up hint is limited per IP and gives only the course name and a masked address, and only for an invitation that is still Invited. No address, request body or exception message is ever logged or sent to Sentry.
